original_value: The design of a computer-supported serious game concerning inhibition skills in children with Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is reported. The game consists of a series of activities, each eliciting the tendency to respond in an immediate, inadequate way. The game is based on the Dual Pathway Model of ADHD proposed by Sonuga-Barke. In the game, children must block impulsive tendencies, reflect upon the situation, inhibit irrelevant thoughts, and find the non-intuitive solution. In the game, the player personifies a superhero, who is asked to save a realm on the opposite side of the Earth (Antonyms) where things happen according to the opposite of the usual rules. The hero faces a series of challenges, in the form of mini-games, to free the planet from enemies crossing different scenarios. To succeed in the game, the player should change his/her attitude by thinking before performing any action rather than acting on impulse. The player is induced to be reflective and thoughtful as well. Results from the evaluation of a preliminary version of the serious game are reported. They support the notion that Antonyms is an adequate tool to lead children to inhibit their tendency to behave impulsively.

result.paraphrase: The paper presents a computer-assisted serious game designed to train inhibition skills in children with Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). It is made up of a sequence of activities that trigger an immediate, inappropriate response. Grounded in Sonuga-Barke’s Dual Pathway Model of ADHD, the game requires children to suppress impulsive tendencies, consider the situation, block irrelevant thoughts, and discover the non-obvious solution. Players take on the role of a superhero tasked with rescuing a world on the far side of the Earth, Antonyms, where events follow rules opposite to the usual ones. The hero must complete a series of mini-game challenges across different scenarios to defeat enemies and free the planet. Success depends on adopting a more reflective mindset and thinking before acting rather than responding on impulse. The paper also reports evaluation results for a preliminary version of the game, which indicate that Antonyms is a suitable tool for helping children inhibit impulsive behavior.
